title: The Pitfalls of Review Solicitation: Evidence from a Natural Experiment on TripAdvisor
eligible_reason: Staggered binary adoption (523 hotels start review solicitation in 61 distinct months, 2010-2017) estimated with Gardner's did2s, but the published specification is a within-hotel cross-platform triple difference: Y_{hpt} on duad(hotel) FE + month FE + trip (platform) + after (hotel-level post indicator) with treatment after_tec = trip x after. The additive `after` term is a time-varying hotel-level regressor (an additional staggered treatment) and the unit FE are hotel + platform dummy, not listing (hotel_id) FE. Under PROTOCOL Section 2 ('additional treatments', 'other nonredundant additive fixed effects', 'time-varying controls') this is not a canonical staggered DiD. Recorded as borderline for lead review.
design_notes: Data: hotel_month_panel.dta, 23,350 hotel-platform-month rows = 1,046 hotel_id (523 hotels x TripAdvisor/Expedia), 75 calendar months 2010-2017, each hotel observed relative_month -12..11 around its own solicitation start (median 48 rows per duad). All 523 hotels are eventually treated; no never-treated hotels in the main sample (ddd_data.dta adds non-participants for appendix Tables A9-A10). after_tec == trip*after verified in data; after never switches off. Outcomes: volume (log(x+1)), average rating, average length (log(x+1)) of all reviews (Table 3), organic reviews (Table 4), reviews by organic reviewers (Table 5). Clustering by duad. Event-study versions (did2s, monthly bins -12..11, omitted -1) only in online appendix Figures A2-A3. If the lead admits DDD-type designs, a canonical mapping exists: units = hotel_id, treatment = after_tec (TripAdvisor listings treated at hotel-specific months, Expedia listings never treated), FE = hotel_id + time, cluster duad; the TWFE/CSA/BJS counterparts can be constructed directly from hotel_month_panel.dta.
estimators_reported: did2s (Gardner two-stage DiD) static, Tables 3-5, 7-8, A1-A12
reghdfe TWFE single-date DiD on CEM-matched reviewers, Table 6

specs.treatment_definition: trip = 1 for the hotel's TripAdvisor listing (0 for its Expedia listing); after = 1 from the month the hotel started review solicitation on TripAdvisor (hotel-specific month, 61 distinct months, 2010-2017). after_tec = trip*after is 1 for TripAdvisor listings after solicitation start.
specs.unit_var: hotel_id (hotel-platform listing); duad = hotel (pair of listings)
specs.assignment_unit: hotel (duad); within hotel only the TripAdvisor listing is treated
specs.fe: first_stage(i.duad i.time trip after): hotel (duad) FE + month FE + platform dummy trip + hotel-level post indicator after
specs.controls: after (hotel-level post-solicitation indicator, time-varying) and trip (platform dummy) as additive regressors
specs.sample_condition: all rows of hotel_month_panel.dta (523 hotels x 2 platforms, 24-month window relative_month -12..11 around each hotel's solicitation start; N=23,350 rows, 20,000-23,350 non-missing depending on outcome)
specs.sample: participating hotels only; all 523 hotels eventually treated on TripAdvisor; Expedia listings never treated
specs.exclusion_reason: triple-difference (DDD): hotel-level post indicator `after` enters as an additional staggered regressor alongside the treatment after_tec = trip x after, and unit FE are duad + trip rather than listing-level (hotel_id) FE. Falls under PROTOCOL exclusions 'additional treatments' / 'other nonredundant additive fixed effects'. Borderline: see screener_notes.

screener_notes: Article text not in the frame (text_path empty); screening based on README, mainresults_code.do, appendix_code.do and the data. Published coefficients therefore not recorded (published_estimates empty); Tables 3-5 can be reproduced exactly from the package. Data are scraped TripAdvisor/Expedia hotel-month panels shipped in the package (hotel_month_panel.dta, 6.9 MB). The eligibility call hinges on whether a within-hotel cross-platform DDD with an additive hotel-level `after` term counts as 'additional treatment'; I classified it as excluded per protocol. If the lead admits it, priority becomes 1 with 9 static main-text specs (Tables 3-5, 3 columns each) and 6 appendix event-study paths; note that the did2s second stage with no never-treated hotels identifies off the Expedia listings only.
